source_name: T-Systems Hungary / Magyar Telekom business ICT – references and payments delivery
why_relevant: Market-leading HU ICT integrator, wholly owned by Magyar Telekom, serving large corporates and public institutions with integration from a single source. Documented role in Hungary's instant/real-time payments go-live alongside ACI Worldwide and Capsys — a direct link between an integrator and national payment infrastructure. Its reference pages and Magyar Telekom's IR reporting expose the financial-sector book.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe – banking portfolio and reference pages
why_relevant: Largest CEE-headquartered software house/system integrator in banking; publishes core-banking and digital-banking product/reference pages plus (via Asseco Poland group IR) segment revenue by country and vertical. Key competitor-and-partner map input for Hungary and neighbouring markets.

source_name: Dorsum Zrt. – HU banking/wealth software vendor references
why_relevant: Budapest-based ~250-person securities/wealth-management software house whose published client list spans major HU financial institutions (OTP, MKB, CIB, Takarék, Raiffeisen, Hungarian State Treasury) and regional offices in RO/BG. Its reference and news pages reveal bank-side project awards that never appear in public procurement.

source_name: Hungarian Fintech Association (HFA / hunfintech.com) member directory
why_relevant: Curated directory of Hungarian fintech and banking-software companies with per-member profile pages describing clients and product lines. The single fastest way to expand the actor map of local fintech dev shops that subcontract to or compete with the large integrators.

source_name: Infoklaszter (IT cluster) member company directory
why_relevant: Hungarian IT cluster listing member companies with capability descriptions. Complements HFA by covering integration/dev shops that are not fintech-branded but subcontract on banking and public-sector IT work.

source_name: e-beszámoló – Elektronikus Beszámoló Portál (Ministry of Justice company filings)
why_relevant: Statutory annual accounts of every Hungarian company, free to search. Lets you size local integrators, fintech dev shops and the HU arms of NTT Data/DXC/Accenture by revenue, headcount cost and profitability, and detect growth that correlates with a big bank or state framework win. Bulk filing datasets are also sold by the Company Information Service.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár / OPTEN company registry data
why_relevant: Commercial company-registry layer with ownership links, registered activity codes, officers and change history — needed to resolve entity aliases (Kft./Zrt./Nyrt. renames, group restructurings such as Takarékinfo, Finshape Hungary Kft.) before matching procurement winner strings to actors.

source_name: Bank outsourcing registers (kiszervezési nyilvántartás) published by HU banks — e.g. CIB Bank
why_relevant: Hungarian credit institutions must publish a register of outsourced activities and the companies performing them (kiszervezés). These annexes name the actual IT service providers, integrators and BPO suppliers behind a bank's operations — the private-sector equivalent of an award notice, and invisible in procurement data.

source_name: MNB Fintech és Digitalizációs Jelentés (central bank fintech & digitalisation report)
why_relevant: The central bank's periodic report quantifies HU bank IT spend, outsourcing/vendor dependence and digitalisation project activity — the denominator against which integrator revenue claims and consultancy studies should be sanity-checked, and a pointer to which technology domains banks are procuring.

source_name: Nádor Rendszerház – közbeszerzés (supplier-side procurement disclosure page)
why_relevant: Example of the supplier-side pattern worth harvesting systematically: HU IT suppliers publish their own procurement/framework participation pages and subcontracting calls. Aggregating these across the integrator actor list reveals framework positions and partner chains not visible in buyer-side notices.

source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (procedure search)
why_relevant: Hungary's mandatory e-procurement platform; state-owned and public-sector merchants (utilities, toll operator, transport, hospitals) run their card-acceptance / VPOS / POS terminal / payment-gateway tenders here. Free-text search on payments terms surfaces acquirer and PSP contracts and their awarded bidders.

source_name: Nemzeti Útdíjfizetési Szolgáltató – VPOS 2025/2026 tender documentation (worked example)
why_relevant: Concrete, recent example of a Hungarian state company procuring virtual POS / online card acceptance (EKR001432572025). Shows the document pattern, CPV codes and requirement language to template future payments-tender detection; also shows contracting authorities publish tender docs on their own sites in parallel with EKR.

source_name: MNB – Nyílt bankoláshoz kapcsolódó pénzforgalmi és harmadik fél szolgáltatók adatai (PSD2 TPP data)
why_relevant: Regulator-maintained actor list of Hungarian PSD2 third-party providers (AISP/PISP) and ASPSPs with contact data — the authoritative universe of TPP actors whose partnerships, RFPs and integrations we must track.

source_name: MNB – Pénzforgalmi intézmények adatszolgáltatás / statisztikák
why_relevant: Supervisory reporting hub for payment institutions; the reported data and periodic payment-system reports reveal acquiring volumes, terminal counts and market shares that indicate when a merchant/acquirer switch or tender wave is likely.

source_name: MNB qvik official site (incl. GYIK / provider info)
why_relevant: Central-bank-owned brand hub for the qvik instant-payment scheme: rules, participating providers, merchant onboarding requirements and logo-display obligations. Changes here (new scheme rules, mandates) are the upstream trigger for acquirer and merchant procurement activity.

source_name: SimplePay (OTP Mobil) – qvik and merchant integration pages
why_relevant: OTP Mobil is one of the first qvik sub-aggregators and the largest HU online acquiring gateway. Its qvik pages, developer docs and press releases announce new integration models, technical-provider partnerships and merchant wins — leading indicators of acquiring share shifts.

source_name: Barion Payment Zrt. – developer documentation & partner pages
why_relevant: Barion is a HU-licensed e-money/payment institution and major domestic gateway; its public docs wiki reveals supported schemes, new products (qvik, instant), partner/reseller programmes and API changes — a reliable early signal of capability and partnership moves.

source_name: Bank merchant-acquiring product & ÁSZF pages (OTP, K&H, MBH, Takarékbank/MBH, Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB)
source_subtype: acquirer product pages and general terms
why_relevant: Acquirer-side terms (ÁSZF), pricing and terminal offerings define the competitive field for merchant acquiring; ÁSZF amendment notices (hirdetmény) are dated, machine-readable evidence of scheme/product changes and of which terminal vendors and schemes each acquirer supports.

source_name: net.jogtar.hu – Hungarian consolidated legislation (e.g. 47/2016 NGM POS terminal subsidy decree)
why_relevant: State subsidy and mandate rules (terminal deployment subsidies, mandatory electronic acceptance obligations) create tender-like allocation processes and force merchant/acquirer contracting. Legal text gives eligibility rules and the responsible administering body to track.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség (Hungarian Fintech Association)
why_relevant: Industry association bundling HU fintech/payments actors; member listings and position papers are a compact actor map and a route to PSPs/TPPs that never appear in procurement portals.

source_name: Mastercard payment facilitator directory
why_relevant: Scheme-maintained list of registered payment facilitators; filtering for Hungary-registered entities reveals PayFacs operating under HU acquirers — actors invisible in MNB registers because they ride an acquirer's licence.

source_name: Visa acceptance-entity / payment facilitator model documentation
why_relevant: Defines the scheme's acceptance-entity taxonomy (acquirer, PayFac, marketplace, sponsored merchant, ISO) that structures how HU acquiring deals are contracted; needed to classify Hungarian actors correctly and to interpret tender requirement language.

source_name: Festipay (event/cashless payments vendor)
why_relevant: Niche HU cashless/event payments provider that wins festival, stadium and venue acceptance contracts — a segment whose 'tenders' are private RFPs and public-venue procurements rather than bank RFPs; useful for widening the acquiring competitor set.

source_name: Terminal reseller / comparison sites (bankkartyaterminalok.hu, posnavigator.eu)
why_relevant: Reseller and comparison sites enumerate which acquirers, terminal hardware brands and gateways are actively sold in Hungary and at what pricing — a fast, if commercially biased, map of the merchant-facing supply side and of switching offers.

source_name: MNB Piaci szereplők keresése (market participant search hub)
why_relevant: Landing hub linking all MNB register sub-searches (general search, intermediaries, special databases). Best single entry point for snowballing to every MNB-held list of actors.

source_name: MNB Közvetítők keresése (intermediary/agent register)
why_relevant: Register of money-market and insurance intermediaries/agents (Hpt./Bit. based). Agents are the distribution layer for payment services and often the counterparties in POS/terminal deployment chains.

source_name: MNB Számlavezető pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók adatai (open banking / ASPSP list)
why_relevant: Enumerates account-servicing PSPs and TPPs with their open-banking/API contact data — a precise, deduplicated target list of the institutions that procure payments technology.
